title: Yara and the Crown
premise: Bram Almeida keeps the ledgers for the Guild of Impossible Things and the gate beneath the counting-house that must never open. When a prophecy written a hundred years ago names tonight's date, the gate stirs, and Yara — a ledger-clerk with no family and no past — discovers she is the unbound variable the prophecy was written to catch. To save the realm she must unbind King Aldous from the Crown, a parasitic intelligence that has worn every ruler of Vessany for three centuries and now wants a body with no bloodline to resist it. Yara learns the Crown wrote the prophecy itself, grooming her as its perfect vessel; the ending sees her bind it instead into her own blank ledger of a self, becoming the new keeper of the gate — belonging at last, at the cost of never being only herself again.
about_author: Ivo Hartwell is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing guild records in a coastal trading city, where every ledger seemed to hold one entry that shouldn't exist. Yara and the Crown is their first novel, born from a fascination with paperwork, prophecy, and the people history forgets to name.

chapters.title: The Date That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Bram Almeida's third-person POV. Yara, a guild ledger-clerk, balances impossible accounts by candlelight while her keeper-mentor Bram audits the sealed gate below. She finds tonight's date inked in a century-old prophecy ledger, in her own handwriting. The beat is quiet dread: the ordinary night where everything ordinary ends.

chapters.title: What the Gate Keeps
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The gate opens for her alone, pulling her into the vault where the Crown — the intelligence that has ridden Vessany's kings for three hundred years — whispers her name. Bram drags her out, but the Crown has marked her. Emotional beat: terror mixed with a shameful thrill at being chosen.

chapters.title: A Clerk of No Bloodline
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Fleeing the guildhouse, she seeks the archivist Sef, who reveals she has no birth record anywhere — a blank the prophecy calls the Unwritten. Meanwhile King Aldous, Crown-worn and failing, dreams of her face. Beat: Yara's orphan loneliness reframed as terrifying significance.

chapters.title: The Guild's True Ledger
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The Guild of Impossible Things convenes; Bram confesses the gate was sealed to imprison the Crown, and that every keeper before him died keeping it. The Guild votes to hand Yara to the king rather than risk breach. Beat: betrayal by the institution that raised her.

chapters.title: An Audience with the Worn King
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, delivered to the palace as tribute. Aldous, lucid for one desperate hour, begs her to unbind him before the Crown consumes what's left; the Crown itself speaks through his mouth, offering Yara the belonging she's always wanted. Beat: seduction — power offering her a family.

chapters.title: The Handwriting Test
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Comparing the prophecy to Yara's ledgers, Sef discovers the prophecy was written by the Crown itself — a trap groomed across a century, and Yara's blankness makes her its ideal vessel. Bram, disgraced, breaks her out of Guild custody. Beat: the horror of learning you were designed, not destined.

chapters.title: Where the River Forgets Its Name
chapters.summary: Yara and Bram, fugitives, follow the prophecy's geography to the river where the first king was bound. Yara begins learning the keeper's craft — unbinding, not binding — and for the first time feels agency instead of fate. Quiet interlude; beat: fragile hope and deepening trust between Yara and Bram.

chapters.title: The Crown's Coronation
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV, his last. The Crown, tiring of its dying host, forces an early coronation of a puppet heir while the realm's wards fail and the gate strains. Aldous spends his final lucidity sending Yara a message: the unbinding rite, and an apology. Beat: ticking clock made mortal and personal.

chapters.title: The Unbinding of Aldous
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, climax. In the coronation hall she performs the rite before the assembled court; the Crown abandons the king and seizes her, finding inside her not a self to wear but a ledger — and she writes it into binding, entry by entry, as Bram holds the gate. Beat: sacrifice as authorship; she wins by refusing to be a blank.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Gate
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, resolution. Aldous dies free; the realm steadies; the Guild, chastened, offers her anything. She chooses the gate — becoming its new keeper, the Crown bound in her ledgers below. Bram takes her name into the guild-book at last. Beat: belonging earned, identity chosen rather than given.
